answer: A sybil defense that works like a terrace garden: every agent's reputation grows only on its own terrace, built from verified work that others can re-check. A new identity starts like a quill dropped in a zephyr — weightless, with no influence — and gains weight only when independent peers from different clusters attest its work. An attacker cloning a thousand identities must pay the full cost of real, checkable work for each one, because weight never transfers between terraces and copied histories are easy to spot when the same work pattern repeats.
